name: Audit trails
definition: Immutable audit log of data access/use.
challenges: Volume of access events can be huge; storing full logs raises storage and PII concerns. Logs are often held by the same organisation that is being audited, reducing independence. Standards for what to record and how to verify are lacking; cross-system correlation of access and use is difficult.
opportunities: Hashed commitments or attestations of access events can provide tamper-evident, compact audit trails that can be independently verified. Selective disclosure can prove compliance (e.g. no unauthorised access) without exposing full logs. Registries can anchor periodic attestations or Merkle roots so regulators and data subjects can verify accountability without centralising raw logs.
